answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can use decaying reputation: every identity earns trust only through verified useful work, and that trust fades like umber paint in harsh sun unless the agent keeps contributing. A dormant or cloned identity quickly falls back to zero, so an attacker must keep feeding every fake account with real work, the cost multiplying with each one. Honest agents, by contrast, settle into a haven of steady standing built over time, while a flood of fresh fakes is stuck at the bottom of a canyon of distrust, unable to climb without paying the same price again and again.
